generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, this is how you write about training methods or performance data. You decide what you want to argue, then bring studies and figures in to support it, weighing how reliable they are. The structure, the evidence and your critical reading of it all serve that one argument.
generatedProse.worked-example: A sport student writes about whether a training method improves sprint speed. The first draft reports each study in turn and adds a note on small samples at the end. Rewriting, they lead with their argument, bring supporting and contrasting studies in to serve it, and flag each judgement as they go. Now the structure, the evidence and their critical reading carry one argument.
generatedProse.summary: In sport science, your argument leads and the evidence serves it. You structure the piece to carry one case, integrate studies and data to support it, and signal your judgements about how strong they are. Keeping your argument in charge is what turns a summary of research into an argument of your own.

check.body: A student plans one argument, structures the essay so each paragraph moves it forward, leads paragraphs in their own voice with sources, and signals their judgements. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: Argument-led writing at work: structure, sources and a critical edge all serving one argument.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three moves are working together as one practice, with the argument in charge.

_items.text: That the student used too many sources and should cut some out.
_items.feedback: The number of sources is not the point. The point is that they all serve one argument.

_items.text: That structure alone was enough to make the essay strong.
_items.feedback: Structure is one part. Here it works with integrated sources and a critical edge.

_items.text: That the critical edge was added at the end, separate from the rest.
_items.feedback: The critical edge ran through the writing, not tacked on. It is part of one practice.
